topics.name: Kinds of sentences and changing them
Passive voice (incl. modals and perfect tenses)

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: We have reduced the number of child labourers.
We have reduce the number of child labourers.
We has reduced the number of child labourers.
questions.rule: Present perfect = have/has + past participle. With 'We', use have reduced.

options: Every child is free to playing and learn.
Every child is free to plays and learn.
Every child is free to play and learn.
questions.rule: An infinitive is to + base verb: to play.

options: No other challenge is as bigger as fear.
No other challenge is as big as fear.
No other challenge is so big than fear.
questions.rule: Positive degree: as + adjective + as (as big as).

options: The children should be send to school.
The children should sent to school.
The children should be sent to school.
questions.rule: Passive with a modal: should + be + past participle (be sent).

options: How brave the little bird fought the fire!
How bravely the little bird fought the fire!
How bravely did the little bird fought the fire!
questions.rule: To describe the action 'fought', use the adverb: How bravely + subject + verb!

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: Kailash Satyarthi founded his movement in 1980.
Kailash Satyarthi has founded his movement in 1980.
Kailash Satyarthi was founded his movement in 1980.
questions.rule: A finished past time (in 1980) takes the simple past, not the present perfect.

options: Governments must invests in education to help poor children.
Governments must invest in education to help poor children.
Governments must invest in education to helping poor children.
questions.rule: After must use the base verb (invest); purpose is shown by to + base verb (to help).

options: The Nobel Prize is greater than most other honour in the world.
The Nobel Prize is more greater than most other honours in the world.
The Nobel Prize is greater than most other honours in the world.
questions.rule: most other takes a plural noun (honours); never use 'more' with '-er' (greater).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Present perfect: have + past participle (have marched).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After to in an infinitive, use the base verb: to accept.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Comparing with all needs the superlative: the biggest.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Passive: was + past participle (was forced).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: In a question with did, the main verb is the base form: did ... ask.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: has + past participle: Has Riya ever forgotten?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Modal passive: must be + past participle (must be made).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: one of the + superlative is followed by a plural noun: speeches.

questions.after: you ever helped a child to read?
questions.rule: With the past participle helped + 'ever', the question begins with Have.

questions.after: never seen such a brave bird.
questions.rule: With I, the present perfect is have + past participle.
want is followed by the infinitive: wanted to put out.
With than, use the comparative: stronger.
Modal passive: can be + past participle (can be restored).

questions.after: kind the volunteers were to us!
questions.rule: Before an adjective alone (kind), the exclamation word is How.

questions.before: Kailash Satyarthi has worked for children's rights
questions.rule: Use since with a starting point in time (1980); for is used with a length of time.

questions.before: Very few rivers in India are as
questions.rule: Between as ... as, use the positive degree: as long as.
An imperative sentence starts with the verb, often after Please.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence in the present perfect.
questions.rule: Subject + have + past participle + object.
free + to + base verb: free to dream.
Present perfect passive: have been + past participle.
the + superlative + noun + I had ever heard.

chat: Have you finished your speech for Children's Day?
questions.rule: Answer in the same tense: I have finished.

chat: How can I help the children at the construction site?
options: You can to teach them to read in the evenings.
You can teach them to read in the evenings.
You can teaching them to read in the evenings.
questions.rule: After can use the base verb without 'to' (teach); after teach them, use 'to read'.

chat: Who built this new school in the village?
options: It was build by a group of volunteers.
It is built by a group of volunteers last year.
It was built by a group of volunteers.
questions.rule: Past passive: was + past participle (was built).

chat: Which was harder, the science paper or the maths paper?
options: The maths paper was more harder than the science paper.
The maths paper was much harder than the science paper.
The maths paper was hardest than the science paper.
questions.rule: Use much (not 'more') to make a comparative stronger: much harder.

chat: I'm going to volunteer at the night school.
options: Yes, I'd love to! What time does it start?
Yes, I'd love to! What time it starts?
Yes, I'd love to! What time does it starts?
questions.rule: Wh-question: What time + does + subject + base verb?

chat: How long have you known Shazia?
options: I have knew her since Class 3.
I have known her since Class 3.
questions.rule: From a past point till now: present perfect have known + since.

chat: Can the old library be used for the night classes?
options: Yes, ma'am. It can cleaned and painted this week.
Yes, ma'am. It can be cleaned and painted this week.
Yes, ma'am. It can be clean and painted this week.
questions.rule: Modal passive: can be + past participle (cleaned, painted).

chat: Why did you start collecting old books?
They are piling up in your room!
options: I want giving them to children who can't afford them.
I want to gave them to children who can't afford them.
I want to give them to children who can't afford them.
questions.rule: want + infinitive: want to give (to + base verb).

options: The world is not so poor.
The world are not so poor.
The world is not so poorly.
questions.rule: A positive rhetorical question becomes a negative statement: The world is not so poor.
How becomes very; keep the participle 'frightened' and the plural verb 'look'.

options: It can be did by us.
It could be done by we.
It can be done by us.
questions.rule: Modal passive: can be + past participle; 'we' becomes by us.

questions.source: Her angry question still shakes me.
options: I am still shaken by her angry question.
I am still shook by her angry question.
I was still shaken by her angry question.
questions.rule: Simple present passive: am/is/are + past participle (am shaken).

questions.source: Fear is the biggest challenge facing humankind.
options: Fear is more bigger than any other challenge facing humankind.
Fear is bigger than any other challenge facing humankind.
Fear is biggest than any other challenge facing humankind.
questions.rule: Superlative to comparative: bigger than any other; never 'more' with an -er word.

questions.source: The Nobel Prize is one of the greatest honours in the world.
options: Very few honours in the world are greater than the Nobel Prize.
Very few honours in the world is as great as the Nobel Prize.
Very few honours in the world are as great as the Nobel Prize.
questions.rule: 'one of the + superlative' becomes Very few ... are as + adjective + as.

questions.source: We have prevented millions of child deaths.
options: Millions of child deaths have been prevented by us.
Millions of child deaths has been prevented by us.
Millions of child deaths have been prevent by us.
questions.rule: Present perfect passive: have been + past participle; plural subject takes 'have'.
The question means 'you ought to have come': should have + past participle.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: have taught (past participle); Last week is finished past time, so simple past joined.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Comparing with a whole school needs the superlative bravest; to + base verb: to become.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: was announced (passive); did ... tell (base verb); 'will be held' takes the tag won't it?

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Modal passive needs past participles: be stopped, be given; 'all of us' is plural: work.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Two weeks ago is past: decided; 'Both my parents' is plural: have agreed; to + base verb: to join.
